newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany plans two-step transition for euro.
newsitem.headline: Germany plans two-step transition for euro.

text.p: The German cabinet on Monday approved plans for the state administration to switch over to using the planned single European currency, the euro, on January 1, 2002.

But, according to an interim report published by the Finance Ministry, companies should be able to convert their equity into euro-denominated shares as soon as the euro is introduced at the start of 1999.
The report also said two models were being considered for redenominating German companies' shares, which have a typical nominal value of five marks, into euros.

One option would be to eliminate the nominal value of shares, which would require small legislative reforms, while the other would be to introduce a standard nominal value for shares of at least one euro.

Although businesses were encouraged to start up transactions in euros from 1999, they will have to continue drawing up their tax returns in deutschemarks for operations until the end of 2001, the paper said.
European monetary union's timetable envisages the launch of the euro as a means of exchange in 1999, but euro notes and coins will not be issued until 2002.

Already decided by the European Council of Ministers in 1995 is that new tradeable government securities will be issued in euros from 1999 onwards. No legislative action is needed here, but legal changes will be needed to convert old debts into euros.
